d_sv_content.name: A Limb-Sparing Option for Bone Cancer in Dogs
d_sv_content.tagline: A personalized 3D-printed implant designed to replace bone and help your dog keep their leg
d_sv_content.description:
This study is evaluating a new limb-sparing surgery for dogs with bone cancer (osteosarcoma). Instead of removing the limb, this approach uses a custom 3D-printed implant to replace the diseased bone.

The implant is designed specifically for your dog using advanced imaging and is made from a material that can gradually be replaced by your dog’s own bone over time. The goal is to maintain limb function while treating the cancer.

Dogs in this study will undergo surgery followed by chemotherapy and long-term monitoring to evaluate how well the implant works and how the cancer responds to treatment.
d_sv_content.requirements: Initial testing to confirm eligibilityWhole-body PET-CT scan to design the implantLimb-sparing surgery and hospitalizationChemotherapy every 3 weeks for 6 treatmentsFollow-up visits including:BloodworkOrthopedic exams and gait analysisX-rays of the limb and chestOngoing monitoring every 2 months for up to 20 months
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Cover the cost of initial diagnostic testing and any additional tests recommended by your veterinarianCover costs of complications beyond what the study providesBring your dog to all required study appointments, including bandage changes (expected to be needed every 1-5 days for 2+ weeks after surgery)Cover costs of any visits performed outside CSUAgree to provide the limb to study personnel after your dog passes away or is euthanized
d_sv_content.whoCan: Dogs may qualify if they:Have suspected or confirmed osteosarcoma of the distal radiusMeet criteria for limb-sparing surgeryAre giant breed or weigh at least 88 lbs (40 kg)Have no evidence of cancer spread (metastasis)Are otherwise healthyAre not receiving medications that affect the immune system
d_sv_content.benefits: Benefits:Access to an advanced limb-sparing surgical optionStudy covers major costs, including:PET-CT scan and anesthesiaCustom 3D-printed implantSurgery and hospitalizationChemotherapy and follow-up imaging for up to 20 monthsUp to $5,825 coverage for surgical complicationsContribute to research that may improve treatment for bone cancer in dogsRisks:Risks associated with major surgery and anesthesiaPossible complications from the implant or healing processSide effects from chemotherapyLong-term commitment for follow-up careTreatment may not be successful
d_sv_content.compensation: Study covers surgery, implant, chemotherapy, and follow-up care, with additional support for complications
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: Initial surgery and chemotherapy over several months, with follow-up visits every 2 months for up to 20 months
